\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.UniformNoiseStability}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function class]
\lean{FABL.BooleanClass}
\label{FABL.BooleanClass}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
A Boolean function class assigns to each natural number $n$ a set of Boolean functions
on $n$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Negation of input variables]
\lean{FABL.negateInputVariables}
\label{FABL.negateInputVariables}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
For a natural number $n$, a sign vector $z\in\{\pm1\}^n$, and a Boolean function
$f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, define a Boolean function by $x\mapsto f((z_i x_i)_{i=1}^n)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Identification of input variables]
\lean{FABL.identifyInputVariables}
\label{FABL.identifyInputVariables}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $\pi:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$ be a map,
and let $f$ map sign vectors of length $n$ to the units of $\mathbb Z$. Define a
function on sign vectors $w$ of length $m$ by $w\mapsto
f\bigl((w_{\pi(i)})_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigr)$; that is, each input coordinate $i$ of $f$ is
assigned the coordinate selected by $\pi(i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Closure under input sign changes]
\lean{FABL.IsClosedUnderNegatingInputVariables}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p131-b002}
\label{FABL.IsClosedUnderNegatingInputVariables}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanClass, FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.negateInputVariables}
A Boolean function class is closed under negating input variables if, for every number
$n$ of coordinates, every input sign vector $z\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and every function $f$ in
the class on $n$ coordinates, the function obtained by negating the input variables
specified by $z$ also belongs to the class on $n$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Closure under identifying input variables]
\lean{FABL.IsClosedUnderIdentifyingInputVariables}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p131-b002}
\label{FABL.IsClosedUnderIdentifyingInputVariables}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanClass, FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.identifyInputVariables}
A Boolean function class is closed under identifying input variables if, for all natural
numbers $n,m$, every map $\pi$ from the $n$ input coordinates to the $m$ input
coordinates, and every function $f$ in the class on $n$ coordinates, the function
obtained by identifying inputs according to $\pi$ belongs to the class on $m$
coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Partition function]
\lean{FABL.partitionFunction}
\label{FABL.partitionFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign
cube to the sign group, let $z$ be a sign vector of length $n$, and let $\pi$ map the
$n$ coordinates to the $m$ coordinates. The partition function associated with $f$, $z$,
and $\pi$ is the function on the $m$-dimensional sign cube that sends each sign vector
$w$ to $f$ evaluated at the vector whose $i$th coordinate is $z_i w_{\pi(i)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Closure under signed variable identification]
\lean{FABL.partitionFunction_mem}
\label{FABL.partitionFunction_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanClass, FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsClosedUnderIdentifyingInputVariables, FABL.IsClosedUnderNegatingInputVariables, FABL.identifyInputVariables, FABL.negateInputVariables, FABL.partitionFunction}
\difficulty{3}
Let $B$ assign to each dimension $k$ a class of functions from the $k$-dimensional sign
cube to ${-1,1}$. Suppose $B$ is closed under independently negating input coordinates
and under identifying input coordinates. Then for every $f\in B_n$, every sign vector
$z\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and every map $\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$, the function
$w\mapsto f\bigl((z_iw_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^n\bigr)$ belongs to $B_m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Half-noise parameter interval]
\lean{FABL.HalfNoiseParameter}
\label{FABL.HalfNoiseParameter}
\leanok
The half-noise parameter interval is the set of real numbers $p$ satisfying $0 \le p \le
\tfrac12$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Unit probability interval]
\lean{FABL.UnitProbability}
\label{FABL.UnitProbability}
\leanok
The unit probability interval is the set of real numbers $p$ satisfying $0 \le p \le 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Positive half-noise parameter interval]
\lean{FABL.PositiveHalfNoiseParameter}
\label{FABL.PositiveHalfNoiseParameter}
\leanok
The positive half-noise parameter interval is the set of real numbers $p$ satisfying $0
< p \le \tfrac12$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Inverse noise floor]
\lean{FABL.inverseNoiseFloor}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p131-b002}
\label{FABL.inverseNoiseFloor}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveHalfNoiseParameter}
For a real noise parameter $\delta$ with $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, the inverse noise floor
is the positive integer $\left\lfloor 1/\delta\right\rfloor$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform noise stability]
\lean{FABL.IsUniformlyNoiseStable}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p006-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p130-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b001
}
\label{FABL.IsUniformlyNoiseStable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanClass, FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.HalfNoiseParameter, FABL.UnitProbability, FABL.noiseSensitivity}
A Boolean function class is uniformly noise stable if there is a function assigning a
probability $\varepsilon(\delta)\in[0,1]$ to each noise parameter
$\delta\in[0,\tfrac12]$, such that $\varepsilon(\delta)$ tends to $0$ as $\delta$ tends
to $0$ through positive values, and every function $f$ in the class, in every dimension,
has noise sensitivity at parameter $\delta$ at most $\varepsilon(\delta)$ for every
$\delta\in[0,\tfrac12]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unit upper bound for noise sensitivity]
\lean{FABL.noiseSensitivity_le_one}
\label{FABL.noiseSensitivity_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.noiseSensitivity, FABL.one_sub_two_mul_mem_Icc, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let
$0\leq\delta\leq1$. The probability that $f$ changes when each coordinate of a uniformly
chosen input is independently flipped with probability $\delta$ is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Bounded input length]
\lean{FABL.HasInputLengthAtMost}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p138-b004}
\label{FABL.HasInputLengthAtMost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanClass, FABL.BooleanFunction}
A Boolean function class has input length at most $N$ if every function in the class on
$n$ coordinates satisfies $n\le N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bounded length noise modulus]
\lean{FABL.boundedInputLengthNoiseModulus}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p138-b004}
\label{FABL.boundedInputLengthNoiseModulus}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HalfNoiseParameter, FABL.UnitProbability}
For a natural number $N$ and a noise parameter $\delta\in[0,\tfrac12]$, the bounded
input length noise modulus is $\min\{1,N\delta\}$, regarded as a number in $[0,1]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing of the bounded input length noise modulus]
\lean{FABL.boundedInputLengthNoiseModulus_tendsto_zero}
\label{FABL.boundedInputLengthNoiseModulus_tendsto_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HalfNoiseParameter, FABL.boundedInputLengthNoiseModulus}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $N$, let $\delta$ range over $[0,1/2]$. The function
$\delta\mapsto\min(1,N\delta)$ tends to $0$ as $\delta$ approaches $0$ through strictly
positive values in $[0,1/2]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform functions and independent outputs]
\lean{FABL.map_uniformFunctionPMF_eq_independentProductPMF}
\label{FABL.map_uniformFunctionPMF_eq_independentProductPMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF_apply, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\iota$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ be finite sets, with $\alpha$ nonempty, and let
$\varphi_i:\alpha\to\beta$ be given for each $i\in\iota$. Choose a function
$a:\iota\to\alpha$ uniformly and map it to the function $i\mapsto\varphi_i(a(i))$.
Its distribution is the product, over $i\in\iota$, of the distributions obtained by
choosing uniformly from $\alpha$ and applying $\varphi_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reciprocal dimension in the unit interval]
\lean{FABL.inverseDimension_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.inverseDimension_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every positive natural number $m$, its reciprocal $1/m$ lies in the interval
$[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A finite sum with one omitted term]
\lean{FABL.sum_fin_ite_ne}
\label{FABL.sum_fin_ite_ne}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $m$ be a natural number, let $j\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, and let $q$ be a nonnegative
extended real number. The sum over all $a\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$ that contributes $0$ at
$a=j$ and $q$ otherwise is $(m-1)q$, where the right-hand side means the sum of $m-1$
copies of $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean sum over the true value]
\lean{FABL.sum_bool_filter_true}
\label{FABL.sum_bool_filter_true}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative extended real number $p$, the sum over the true element of the
Boolean set, restricted to the Boolean value that is true, of the weight that is $p$ at
true and $1-p$ at false equals $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean sum over the false value]
\lean{FABL.sum_bool_filter_false}
\label{FABL.sum_bool_filter_false}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative extended real number $p$, the sum over the false element of the
Boolean set, restricted to the Boolean value that is false, of the weight that is $p$ at
true and $1-p$ at false equals $1-p$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}$. Under the coordinate noise rule that keeps
its input sign with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flips it otherwise, the probability of
obtaining $-x$ from $x$ is $1-(1+\rho)/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate flip and noise distribution]
\lean{FABL.map_uniformFin_fiberFlip_eq_coordinateNoisePMF}
\label{FABL.map_uniformFin_fiberFlip_eq_coordinateNoisePMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_neg', FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_self', FABL.correlationKeepProbability, FABL.correlationKeepProbability_le_one, FABL.inverseDimension_mem_Icc, FABL.one_sub_two_mul_mem_Icc, FABL.sum_fin_ite_ne, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m$ be a positive natural number, let $j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$, and let
$x\in\{-1,1\}$. Choose $a$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and output $-x$ if
$a=j$, and $x$ otherwise. The resulting probability distribution is the coordinate noise
distribution at $x$ with correlation parameter $1-2/m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Partition flips induce a noise kernel]
\lean{FABL.map_uniformPartition_eq_noiseKernel}
\label{FABL.map_uniformPartition_eq_noiseKernel}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.inverseDimension_mem_Icc, FABL.map_uniformFin_fiberFlip_eq_coordinateNoisePMF, FABL.map_uniformFunctionPMF_eq_independentProductPMF, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.one_sub_two_mul_mem_Icc, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers with $m>0$, choose a label $j$ among the $m$ labels, and
fix a sign vector $x$ on $n$ coordinates. Choose uniformly a map from the $n$
coordinates to the $m$ labels, and negate $x_i$ exactly at coordinates mapped to $j$.
The resulting random sign vector has the noise-kernel distribution with correlation
parameter $1-2/m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Partition-fiber sign flip]
\lean{FABL.flipPartitionFiber}
\label{FABL.flipPartitionFiber}
\leanok
Given natural numbers $n,m$, a sign vector $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, a map
$\pi:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, and an index $j\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, define a
new sign vector by reversing $x_i$ when $\pi(i)=j$ and leaving it unchanged otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Partition-function flip identity]
\lean{FABL.expect_partitionFunction_flip}
\label{FABL.expect_partitionFunction_flip}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.flipPartitionFiber, FABL.partitionFunction, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $f$ map sign vectors of length $n$ to signs, let
$pi:bfntobfm$ be a coordinate map, and choose a sign vector $w$ of length $m$ and an
index $j<m$. The uniform probability over sign vectors $z$ of length $n$ that the values
of the partition function at $w$ and at the vector obtained by flipping coordinate $j$
differ equals the uniform probability over sign vectors $x$ of length $n$ that $f(x)$
differs from its value after flipping every coordinate $i$ for which $pi(i)=j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Partition flips and noise sensitivity]
\lean{FABL.expect_flipPartitionFiber_eq_noiseSensitivity}
\label{FABL.expect_flipPartitionFiber_eq_noiseSensitivity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.flipPartitionFiber, FABL.inverseDimension_mem_Icc, FABL.map_uniformPartition_eq_noiseKernel, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.noiseSensitivity, FABL.one_sub_two_mul_mem_Icc, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_bind, FABL.pmfExpectation_map, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\geq 1$, choose an index $j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$.
Choose a map from the $n$ coordinates to $m$ labels uniformly at random, and
independently choose $x$ uniformly from the sign cube. The probability that $f(x)$
changes when the signs at coordinates assigned label $j$ are flipped, averaged over both
choices, equals the noise sensitivity of $f$ at noise rate $1/m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average influence equals noise sensitivity]
\lean{FABL.expect_partitionFunction_averageInfluence_eq_noiseSensitivity}
\label{FABL.expect_partitionFunction_averageInfluence_eq_noiseSensitivity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.averageCoordinateFlipProbability, FABL.expect_flipPartitionFiber_eq_noiseSensitivity, FABL.expect_partitionFunction_flip, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.flipPartitionFiber, FABL.inverseDimension_mem_Icc, FABL.noiseSensitivity, FABL.partitionFunction, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers with $m>0$, and let $f\colon\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. Choose
a sign vector $z$ uniformly and a map $\pi\colon\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,1\ldots,m\}$
uniformly and independently. The expected average, over the input coordinates, of the
uniform probability that the partitioned function $w\mapsto f((z_iw_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^n)$
changes when one coordinate of $w$ is flipped equals the noise sensitivity of $f$ at
noise rate $1/m$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ assign to each natural number $r$ a class of Boolean functions on the
$r$-dimensional sign cube. Suppose $B$ is closed under negating input coordinates and
under identifying input coordinates. Let $A$ assign a real number to each positive
natural number, and suppose every $g\in B_r$ has total influence at most $A(r)$. Then,
for every natural number $n$, every $f\in B_n$, and every positive natural number $m$,
the noise sensitivity of $f$ at rate $1/m$ is at most $A(m)/m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise sensitivity bound for a Boolean class]

\difficulty{4}
Let $B=(B_r)_{r\geq0}$ be a class of sign-valued functions on finite sign cubes, closed
under negating input coordinates and under identifying input coordinates. Suppose $A$
assigns a real number to each positive integer $r$, and every $g\in B_r$ has total
influence at most $A(r)$. For any nonnegative integer $n$, any $f\in B_n$, and any
$0<\delta\leq\tfrac12$, the probability that $f$ changes when each coordinate of a
uniformly chosen input is independently flipped with probability $\delta$ is at most
$A(m)/m$, where $m=\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$.
\end{theorem}
